2608.06366.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
2608.06366.paper_summary: Electronic health record (EHR) feature engineering is a major bottleneck in clinical research and AI, accounting for 39-45% of data scientists' workload. This is especially pronounced in heart failure, which affects an estimated 6.7 million U.S. adults and requires integrating fragmented EHR data with disease-specific, guideline-based clinical reasoning. Existing rule-based and large language model (LLM)-based approaches offer only partial automation with limited maintainability and evidence traceability. We developed the Nimblemind Multi-Agent System (nMAS), an evidence-linked, rubric-grounded pipeline for automated heart-failure feature engineering, and evaluated it on 500 dummy patient records from nine EHR source tables. nMAS generated 132 structured and 70 rubric-scored aggregated features, verified for structural integrity, rubric compliance, and provenance, and audited by a restricted LLM. Adding the aggregated features improved held-out AUROC from 0.895 to 0.963 for HFrEF and 0.870 to 0.910 for HFpEF phenotyping, and an independent LLM-based rubric assessment of evidence support and methodological soundness scored the features at 81.5% of maximum points. These results demonstrate the feasibility of automated, auditable feature engineering for complex cardiovascular EHR data, though evaluation was limited to a single-institution cohort and external validation is needed.
2608.06366.paper_summary_zh: 電子健康紀錄（EHR）特徵工程是臨床研究和人工智慧中的主要瓶頸，佔據了數據科學家39-45%的工作量。這在心臟衰竭中尤為明顯，該病影響約670萬名美國成年人，並需要將分散的EHR數據與特定疾病的、基於指南的臨床推理整合。現有的基於規則和大型語言模型（LLM）的方法僅提供有限的自動化，且維護性和證據可追溯性有限。我們開發了Nimblemind多代理系統（nMAS），這是一個基於證據連結和評分標準的自動化心臟衰竭特徵工程管道，並在來自九個EHR源表的500個虛擬病歷上進行了評估。nMAS生成了132個結構化特徵和70個根據評分標準計分的聚合特徵，並驗證了其結構完整性、評分標準合規性和來源，並由一個受限的LLM進行審計。添加聚合特徵後，HFrEF的持出AUROC從0.895提高到0.963，HFpEF表型從0.870提高到0.910，且獨立的基於LLM的評分標準對證據支持和方法論合理性的評估為特徵打分81.5%的滿分。這些結果展示了對於複雜心血管EHR數據進行自動化、可審計特徵工程的可行性，儘管評估僅限於單一機構的隊列，並且需要外部驗證。
